2. Answering questions: The robot can respond to inquiries such as "Where is my child?" or "When should I take the pill?", providing practical assistance and reducing anxiety for users.

3. Tracking repetitive utterances: This function helps to identify potential cognitive issues, allowing the robot to calm the user if needed, thus enhancing emotional support.

4. Providing actions like greetings, conversations, and schedule reminders: These actions contribute to social interaction and help users stay organized, improving their overall well-being.

document: 557_enrichme perception and interaction of an assistive robot for the elderly at home
involved_stakeholder:
Elderly people, caregivers, technical solution providers

Source: "The Polish pilot site was managed by the Poznan University of Medical Science (PUMS), which includes a multi-professional team (geriatrician, nurse, physiotherapist, occupational therapist, dietitian, social workers) specialized in care for older individuals."
sample_size:
N/A

Source: "the second participant’s house between the 15th of January and the 11th of March in 2018."
country:
Greece, Poland

Source: "Two of the participants in Greece chose to name the robots after Greek gods. [...] Also in Poland the participants in the pilot sites chose to personalize the robots..."
age:
The age range is from 66 to 89 years.

Source: "There were 4 women aged from 73 to 89 years, who quickly familiarized with the use of the robot and the its interface." and "the participants were all male and aged 70, 71, and 90, respectively."
demographic_background:
The demographic background information reported includes the ages of the elderly participants, which ranged from 66 to 89 years. It mentions that there were 3 females and 1 male in the Polish pilot site, and in the UK testing sites, the participants were all male aged 70, 71, and 90. Additionally, it notes that only one of the users was already familiar with computer-based technology, and two had some vision impairment.

Source: "The Polish pilot site was managed by the Poznan University of Medical Science (PUMS), which includes a multi-professional team... Here, 4 participants tested the ENRICHME system in their own houses or apartments... There were 3 females and 1 male, with ages between 66 and 83... The UK testing sites... were three 'housing with extra care' schemes... The participants were all male and aged 70, 71, and 90, respectively. Only one of the users was already familiar with computer-based technology, and two of them had some vision impairment."
needs_and_expectations:
The explicitly stated or inferred needs and expectations of users, primarily elderly people and caregivers, include the need for personalized care, cognitive stimulation, social interaction, and ease of use of the robotic system. Users expressed a desire for functionalities that help them cope with loneliness, maintain cognitive abilities, and receive reminders for daily activities.

Source: "the participants pointed out that, when the robot was present, there was 'someone' to talk to, waiting for them at home, and making the environment more friendly. This made easier for them to cope with loneliness." and "the robot was very helpful to improve the users’ diet by providing reminders for snacks or meals during the day, and by recommending the type of food that the user was required to eat."
application_context:
The envisioned application context for the robot is to provide health monitoring, complementary care, and social support for elderly people at home.

Source: "The project’s main goal is to enrich the day-to-day experience of elderly people at home with technologies that enable health monitoring, complementary care, and social support."
process_of_the_care:
The study involved long-term deployment, with participants using the system for approximately 10 weeks. For the first participant, the GUI applications were used in 21 days out of 56 days, with an average interaction time of 45 minutes and a maximum of 166 minutes. The second participant used the GUI applications in 44 days, with an average interaction time of 32 minutes and a maximum of 197 minutes.

Source: "The validation period for each participant lasted approximately 10 weeks... For the first participant, the GUI applications were used in 21 days out of the total 56 days. The average interaction time was of 45 min with a maximum of 166 min... The second participant used the GUI applications in 44 days. The average interaction time was of 32 min with a maximum of 197 min."

N/A

Personalized care for the elderly, specifically mental and physical stimulation.

Source: "Multiple research projects have been focused on providing personalized care for the elderly, more specifically mental and physical stimulation."

The robot used in the study is described as a mobile assistive robot.

Source: "The mobile robot in ENRICHME is particularly useful for two tasks: RFID object mapping and user monitoring."
robot_name:
ENRICHME robot

Source: "This paper described the robotic system implemented by the ENRICHME project to enable health monitoring, complementary care and social support for elderly people at home."
design_goal:
The design goals set by the solution provider included providing services such as domestic monitoring, object finding, personalized reminders, and cognitive games.

Source: "the latter were defined with the active participation of elderly people and formal/informal carers [17], highlighting the need of services such as domestic monitoring, object finding, personalized reminders and cognitive games."
robot_concern_function:
The functionalities of the robot demonstrated, deployed, or introduced to users during the study included cognitive games, health tips, physical activities, object finding, environmental data monitoring, agenda management, video calling, weather forecasting, and news reading.

Source: "The GUI features eight custom developed applications: Cognitive games, Health tips, Physical activities, Find object, Environmental data (i.e., robot sensors; house sensors), Agenda, Call somebody, Weather forecast and News reading."
facilitating_functions:
The specific robot functions or features reported to enhance the user experience include:

1. **Appearance and Functionalities**: Participants highly appreciated the robot's appearance and functionalities, which contributed to a positive perception of the robot.
   
2. **Cognitive Games**: The robot provided various cognitive games that engaged users, helping to maintain and improve their cognitive abilities.

3. **Health Tips**: The robot offered personalized health tips, which were found to be very useful for improving users' nutritional status.

4. **Find Object Feature**: This feature allowed users to locate lost objects around the house, enhancing their independence and reducing frustration.

5. **Environmental Monitoring**: The robot could check home air quality, which users found particularly useful for maintaining a healthy living environment.

Source: "the participants of the validation phase, after familiarizing themselves with the robot, highly appreciated its appearance and functionalities... All four participants enjoyed having the robot in their rooms, playing the cognitive games... the guidelines provided by the healthy-tips application were found very useful... the user can use the ENRICHME robot to localize different objects around the house... they also found the possibility to check the home air quality with the robot on-board sensors particularly useful."
engagement:
The evaluation of user engagement in the robot reported in the study indicates high engagement and acceptance. Participants rated the usefulness, perceived ease of use, perceived enjoyment, and intention to repeat use highly. 

Source: "usefulness, perceived ease of use, perceived enjoyment and intention to repeat use were rated highly by the participants."
acceptance:
The study reports high acceptance of the ENRICHME robot among participants, with quantitative measurements indicating high ratings for usefulness, perceived ease of use, perceived enjoyment, and intention to repeat use.

Source: "usefulness, perceived ease of use, perceived enjoyment and intention to repeat use were rated highly by the participants."
key_findings:
The study found that the ENRICHME robot effectively improved the nutritional status of elderly users, enhanced cognitive engagement through various games, and provided social support, thereby reducing feelings of loneliness. Participants appreciated the robot's functionalities and customization, indicating a positive impact on their daily lives.

Source: "Although the emphasis of this paper is on the enabling technological innovations of our assistive robot, future work should look at opportune methodologies to evaluate the original expectations and the actual experiences of our elderly users... the participants were happy with the robot customization and interaction capabilities."
testing_context:
The testing context of the study was in elderly residences, specifically in facilities operated by the AKTIOS Group in Greece, LACE Housing in the UK, and the Poznan University of Medical Science (PUMS) in Poland.

Source: "In total, six ENRICHME systems were deployed in elderly residences of the pilot sites: two in Greece, two in UK, and two in Poland."

There is also an expectation for robots to stimulate communication among elderly individuals and assist caregivers in managing their workload.

Source: "Communicative robots can stimulate elderly individuals to activate a communication link with others... Automatic recording of vital information using robot sensors can improve the quality of nursing care work."

The envisioned application context for the robot is in caring for elderly individuals, particularly in nursing homes and at home, to address the increased demand for elderly care and the anticipated caregiver shortage in Japan.

Source: "the purpose of this study was to identify the tasks and problems associated with the deployment of communicative robots and a monitoring system for medical care in facilities as well as patients' homes because this technology has been discussed as a means of addressing the increased elderly care demand and the anticipated caregiver shortage in Japan."

The study involved a pilot before-after trial conducted over a period from April to June 2015, indicating a short-term use of the communicative robots and monitoring sensors.

The study suggests that communicative robots can stimulate elderly individuals to activate communication links, reduce the burden on nursing care workers during night shifts, improve the quality of nursing care work through automatic recording of vital information, prevent deterioration of activities of daily living, and that care professionals gradually accepted the robots as assistants.
